nodes.label: Compact rail spec
nodes.rationale: Labels stay in the DOM for accessible names and fade faster than the rail so words are not clipped mid-letter.

nodes.label: Lenis smooth scrolling
nodes.rationale: Motion was rejected as a frame-loop driver because the site animates pointer input, and scrollToTop must route through Lenis so its internal position cannot snap back.

nodes.label: Mobile and theme spec
nodes.rationale: The dialog stays active through dismissal so tapping the toggle while closing reopens immediately instead of waiting for an exit.

nodes.label: Shelf input behavior
nodes.rationale: Hover styling stays plain CSS so artwork responds before hydration, and a scroll-settle re-arms the quote so a resting pointer does not lose its reveal.

nodes.label: Blob buddy interaction limits
nodes.rationale: A 24px neutral zone and 240px response radius with 5 degree tilt and 3px pupil travel keep tracking alive without jitter at the center.

nodes.label: Personal portrait interaction
nodes.rationale: One proportional image scale with automatic height prevents the source photo from stretching at small print sizes.

nodes.label: Personal signature interaction
nodes.rationale: Draw once at 80% visibility and never replay, so the signature stays a first-arrival moment; the documented clip-mask rectangles and 1860ms total predate the implemented stroke-dashoffset approach in DESIGN.md.

nodes.label: Contact modal interaction
nodes.rationale: The sidebar pill and every page CTA open the same dialog so destinations and focus behavior stay in one place.

nodes.label: Magnetic contact controls spec
nodes.rationale: Liquid Gooey Move is limited to a rigid silhouette and 10% press squish so the control reads as magnetically pulled rather than liquid.

nodes.label: Production build EPERM retry
nodes.rationale: The first sandboxed build could not write output; the retry with filesystem access passed TypeScript and static prerendering, so build failure was environmental.

nodes.label: Shelf fit regression at 1440, 1280 and 1001px
nodes.rationale: Asserts scrollWidth stays within clientWidth, all five covers stay inside Shelf bounds, and the open-book reveal adds no horizontal overflow, because the earlier failure was clipping rather than layering.

nodes.label: Ship disposition scoped to scored fixes
nodes.norm_label: ship disposition scoped to scored fixes
nodes.rationale: A scoped ship keeps the review honest about unexamined states while still unblocking the verified corrections.

nodes.label: Greeting and Shelf correction milestone
nodes.rationale: Alan's screenshots overrode a prior visual-review conclusion, so supplied captures outrank an earlier verdict for the states they show.

nodes.label: Responsive rail and character adaptation
nodes.rationale: Below 1000px the hamburger replaces the rail, so Home needs a dedicated character column that desktop does not use; About drops the character entirely.

nodes.label: Direction contract: the projects lead
nodes.rationale: A quieter rail and short professional introduction exist to give project previews room, so hierarchy is decided before styling.

nodes.label: Refinement quality bar
nodes.rationale: Requires no page-wide overflow across eight widths and continued work for greeting, Shelf, portrait, blob and contact states, so a visual win cannot trade away interactions.

nodes.label: Desktop Shelf fitting correction
nodes.rationale: Scales artwork, hit areas and reveal offsets by one container unit so all five items fit above 1000px while text sizes and quote behavior stay untouched; this brief records 16px gaps and a 112px reserve, while DESIGN.md records 32px gaps and a 176px reserve.

nodes.label: Bubble and Shelf browser verification record
nodes.norm_label: bubble and shelf browser verification record
nodes.rationale: Records executed Playwright output rather than a summary claim, so the 15-of-16 full run and the isolated retry can both be audited.

nodes.label: Bubble and Shelf verdict
nodes.rationale: Scores the six requested corrections individually so ship status attaches to the scoped fixes, not to the whole surface.

nodes.label: Portfolio layout refinement brief
nodes.rationale: Binds the approved direction to a fixed contract before implementation, then records what was actually built and corrected.

nodes.label: Six desktop and mobile finish captures
nodes.norm_label: six desktop and mobile finish captures
nodes.rationale: Covers 1440px, 1280px and 390px on both pages plus a first-viewport preview, so fidelity is judged from the top of the document at each breakpoint.

nodes.label: Persistence gate without PRODUCT.md
nodes.rationale: PRODUCT.md is absent, so the review allows only a narrow refinement of the incumbent identity and blocks a replacement visual world or comp.

nodes.label: Portfolio refinement finish review
nodes.rationale: Independent review of the authorized Home and About refinement against six captures and 15 passing Playwright tests.

nodes.label: Keep list of identity features
nodes.rationale: Names the assets and behaviors that later edits must not erode, so refinement cannot quietly remove the site's character.

nodes.label: Soft speech bubble treatment
nodes.rationale: Soft bubbles related to the Blob buddy replaced the rejected dark cards and accent lines, so the quotes read as the Shelf speaking.

nodes.label: Magnetic arrow reduced-motion test retry
nodes.rationale: The full run timed out waiting for data-enhanced on an already visible arrow; the component and test were untouched before an isolated retry passed, so the record treats it as ordering flake, not a regression.

nodes.label: Sticky cursor removal
nodes.rationale: The custom cursor was removed while the magnetic and gooey controls stayed, keeping native input the single pointer truth.

nodes.label: Blob life update
nodes.rationale: Scheduled quick, double and slow blinks replace the fixed 8.6 second loop so the rhythm stops feeling metronomic.

nodes.label: Portrait early-tap guard
nodes.rationale: The effect now reads saved state on mount because a tap can land after hydration but before the spring subscribes.

nodes.label: Dark mode milestone
nodes.rationale: A full token swap plus a pre-paint inline script means a saved dark visit never flashes white, and the 240ms paint-only fade keeps pointer input live.

nodes.label: Proposed larger project presentation
nodes.rationale: Try 3:2 or 16:10 framing, legible interface detail, consistent margins and useful role/context captions without inventing outcomes.
nodes.source_location: ### 1. Make selected work the main visual attraction

nodes.label: Availability Status Indicator
nodes.rationale: A small saturated blue mark sits in the top-right of the identity header. It is the only strong chromatic accent on the page, which is what makes it read as live status rather than decoration.

nodes.label: Expanded Sidebar Navigation Rail
nodes.rationale: The expanded state shows labels next to every affordance; the collapse control at the bottom implies an alternate icon-only rail, so labels are progressive information rather than permanent structure.

nodes.label: Experience Timeline List
nodes.rationale: Each entry stacks employer in bold, then title in muted regular weight beneath it, with the date range floated to the far right. Reading order is reverse-chronological, most recent role first, and no logos or descriptions are used, keeping scanning cost low.

nodes.label: Personal Hero Intro Block
nodes.rationale: An oversized conversational greeting ('Hi, I'm Alan!') followed by two short first-person paragraphs. The voice is spoken and plain, closer to an introduction at a meetup than a professional summary.

nodes.label: Sidebar Identity Header (Name, Role, Avatar)
nodes.rationale: Name in medium-weight display type, role set in a smaller grey line directly under it, and the pixel avatar placed in the slot to the right. The stack reads top-down as who, then what they do, before any navigation appears.

nodes.label: Pixel-Art Avatar Illustration
nodes.rationale: A full-body pixel-art character stands centered in the rail with generous empty space above and below. It carries personality where a real photograph would be too formal, and keeps the rail visually lighter than the content column.

nodes.label: Rounded Portrait Photo Card
nodes.rationale: A vertical 3:4 portrait sits flush to the right gutter of the hero, framed by a very large corner radius with no shadow and no border. Its height roughly matches the greeting plus body copy, so the hero reads as one balanced band.

nodes.label: Sidebar Footer Controls (Collapse, Theme Toggle)
nodes.rationale: Two circular 40px icon buttons pinned to the bottom-left: a double-chevron collapse affordance and a moon glyph for theme. They are deliberately small and desaturated because they are utility, not destination.

nodes.label: Two-Column Sidebar Plus Content Shell
nodes.rationale: Layout splits into an approximately 300px fixed rail and a wide content column, with the content column starting below the top of the sidebar. The sidebar never competes vertically with the article, so identity stays in view while reading long sections.

nodes.label: Sidebar Expanded Reference Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Full-page reference capture of the portfolio's expanded left sidebar state at 1440x900, used as the visual spec for the persistent desktop navigation. Establishes the desktop-first layout where identity and navigation live in a fixed rail while content scrolls independently to the right.

nodes.label: Right-Aligned Date Range Column
nodes.rationale: Durations are set in small muted type and right-aligned to the content column edge rather than inline after the title. The fixed right edge makes tenure comparable at a glance across rows of different title lengths.

nodes.label: Generous Whitespace and Open Leading
nodes.rationale: Body copy is set at a comfortable measure with roughly 1.7 leading, and vertical gaps between blocks are large enough that sections never touch. Density is intentionally low so the page reads as editorial rather than as a dashboard.

nodes.label: Hairline Row Divider
nodes.rationale: One-pixel low-contrast rules separate experience rows and also split the sidebar nav from the CTA group. They substitute for cards and containers, so the page has structure without a single visible box.

nodes.label: Pill Nav Item with Active State
nodes.norm_label: pill nav item with active state
nodes.rationale: Nav rows are full-width pills with a hairline icon on the left and a label to its right. The active row ('Know me better') fills with a soft warm grey instead of a border or underline, so state is legible at low contrast and never shifts layout.

nodes.label: Dark Filled Primary CTA (Get in touch)
nodes.norm_label: dark filled primary cta (get in touch)
nodes.rationale: Fully rounded pill in near-black with white text and a speech-bubble icon. It is the single highest-contrast element in the rail, which makes the contact action the loudest thing above the fold without using color.

nodes.label: Light Surface Secondary CTA (See my resume)
nodes.norm_label: light surface secondary cta (see my resume)
nodes.rationale: Same pill geometry as the primary button but filled with the muted surface grey and dark text. Identical shape plus a one-step value drop creates hierarchy without introducing a second accent color.

nodes.label: Warm Monochrome Palette
nodes.rationale: Near-white canvas, warm off-white surfaces for pills and buttons, and near-black text. Color is spent only on the availability dot and the portrait photograph, so imagery and status carry all the saturation on the page.

nodes.label: 3D Character Avatar Illustration
nodes.rationale: Illustrated avatar instead of a photograph signals a crafted, personal brand and softens an otherwise typographic page.

nodes.label: Capability Tags (Product design, Design systems, Prototyping)
nodes.norm_label: capability tags (product design, design systems, prototyping)
nodes.rationale: Unboxed text separated by thin dividers keeps the skills scannable without chip clutter.

nodes.label: Circular Arrow Button
nodes.rationale: Circle echoing the blob language on the opposite side of the panel balances the block and gives the panel a single unambiguous action.

nodes.label: Client Roster (Daikin Singapore, Thai Honda, SP Group Singapore)
nodes.norm_label: client roster (daikin singapore, thai honda, sp group singapore)
nodes.rationale: Named enterprise clients substitute for unavailable case studies, borrowing their brand recognition as evidence.

nodes.label: Gooey Contact CTA in Pressed State
nodes.norm_label: gooey contact cta in pressed state
nodes.rationale: Dark filled pill is the only high-contrast control in the rail, so pressed feedback (scale and shape compression) carries the gooey deformation without extra chrome.

nodes.label: Have Something in Mind? Contact Panel
nodes.norm_label: have something in mind? contact panel
nodes.rationale: Wide tinted rounded panel is the only large surface with a background color, ending the page on the conversion action; copy reframes contact as a conversation rather than a form.

nodes.label: Current Role Entry: CADIT, UI/UX Designer, Oct 2025 to present
nodes.norm_label: current role entry: cadit, ui/ux designer, oct 2025 to present
nodes.rationale: Two-column split places statement and current employment side by side, so credibility is visible without scrolling to a separate resume page.

nodes.norm_label: footer utility bar (edition, local time, social links)
nodes.rationale: Low-contrast metadata row keeps the page ending quiet after the conversion block; the timezone clock adds presence and signals availability.

nodes.norm_label: blue gooey blob orb (top-right floating trigger)
nodes.rationale: Blob-like silhouette with soft asymmetric edges is the gooey motif; it reads as a living object rather than a button, inviting a press.

nodes.norm_label: homepage shell (fixed sidebar plus scrolling content)

nodes.norm_label: identity header: name plus role sentence

nodes.label: Persistent Sidebar Navigation
nodes.rationale: Keeps navigation, identity and the primary contact action in one fixed column so the call to action stays reachable at any scroll depth; the active item uses a filled pill instead of a color change.

nodes.norm_label: project showcase strip (pet app and meal-planning app imagery)

nodes.label: See My Resume Secondary CTA

nodes.label: Muted attribution line
nodes.rationale: Speaker name (Eames) sits below the quote at a smaller size and lower opacity blue-gray, with no title, role, or punctuation. Hierarchy is achieved by size and color only, which keeps the block compact.

nodes.norm_label: cropped speaker portrait at card edge

nodes.norm_label: quote typography with curly quotation marks
nodes.rationale: Two-line quote set in a humanist sans at a comfortable reading size, dark slate blue, medium weight, generous line height. Typographic curly quotes are part of the content styling rather than added by the component. Generous left padding indents the text from the bubble edge.

nodes.label: Centered speech-bubble tail
nodes.rationale: A small notch protruding from the bubble's bottom edge, centered under the text block rather than under an avatar. It reads as a speech bubble without needing a drawn pointer, keeping the card flat and low-noise.

nodes.label: Accent Palette (Indigo, Ink, Pale Blue)
nodes.rationale: Three colours do all the work: a saturated indigo for the header avatar glyph, near-black ink for headings and the circular arrow button, and a pale desaturated blue for the contact card fill. Everything else is white and grey.

nodes.label: Single-Column Mobile Scroll
nodes.rationale: One content column with consistent horizontal gutters, and every section separated by a hairline plus a large vertical gap (roughly 40-56px). The only element that breaks the column is the media rail's horizontal overflow.

nodes.label: About Page, Mobile Implementation
nodes.rationale: A tall mobile screenshot of the site's About page for Alan Sahlan, a product designer. The page is a single vertical scroll of stacked text-led sections separated by hairline rules: identity header, intro, experience, curated media, personal note, current work, closing note, contact card, footer. Purpose is to prove the implemented mobile layout against the design reference.

nodes.label: Closing Signoff ('Sincerely,')
nodes.rationale: Two-line bold statement followed by 'Sincerely,' on its own line with generous trailing whitespace. The letter-style sign-off is what makes the page read as correspondence rather than a portfolio template.

nodes.label: 'Say hi?' Contact Card
nodes.rationale: Full-width rounded card with a pale blue tint, the only tinted surface on the page. Large heading, muted two-line supporting copy, and a black circular arrow button pinned to the top-right of the card. The arrow is the single high-contrast action affordance in the whole scroll.

nodes.label: Curated Media Rail ('A few things I keep coming back to')
nodes.norm_label: curated media rail ('a few things i keep coming back to')
nodes.rationale: Section heading wraps to two lines with a handwritten-script subtitle 'Pick something up.' below it. Content is a horizontal rail of two off-white square media cards (a film still and a 'KILLERS OF THE FLOWER MOON' poster) that overflow past the right edge, signalling swipeable horizontal scroll. Whitespace above and below is deliberately large to separate it from the experience list.

nodes.label: Still Figuring Things Out Section
nodes.rationale: Heading plus a three-sentence paragraph that names CADIT and frames the site as a learning artifact built with AI. This is the one place the page states its own purpose, so it carries most of the meta narrative.

nodes.label: Experience Timeline
nodes.rationale: Section titled 'Experience' with four stacked entries (CADIT, Freelance, Digistar Class Telkom, Startup Campus). Each entry uses a strict three-tier hierarchy: bold company name, muted role, muted month-range. Hairline divider between every row, no cards or logos, which keeps the list scannable at narrow widths.

nodes.label: Footer Meta Row
nodes.rationale: Three low-contrast items in one row: copyright '2026 (c) Edition', a location pin with 'Indonesia, 10:07 AM GMT+7' (a live clock), then a second row of small square social icons (LinkedIn, Instagram, Behance). The live local time is a small personal touch rather than standard footer furniture.

nodes.label: Header Identity Bar
nodes.rationale: Two-line lockup on the left (name in semibold, role in muted small text) with a solid indigo rounded mascot/avatar glyph, a circular theme toggle showing a moon icon, and a circular hamburger menu on the right. Establishes the sticky-looking top chrome without any border.

nodes.label: Hero Intro: 'Hi, I'm Alan!'
nodes.rationale: Large display heading sits beside a rounded-corner portrait card on the right, which pushes the heading into a narrow measure. A small locate/pin icon plus 'Bandung, Indonesia' precedes two short paragraphs of origin story. The portrait card uses a soft white ring/frame, the only elevated surface in this section.

nodes.label: Off-Screen Personal Note
nodes.rationale: Single muted paragraph ('Away from the screen: coffee, lifting weights, and keeping up with the NBA.') framed by two hairline rules. No heading, so it reads as an aside between two larger sections rather than a section of its own.

nodes.label: First-Person Conversational Voice
nodes.rationale: Every section speaks in plain first person with short sentences and soft hedges ('That's where this all started for me', 'Long story short, here we are', 'Anyway, that's a bit of me'). The voice is the through-line that keeps a stack of unrelated sections feeling like one person talking, so content decisions should be judged against it.

nodes.label: Type-Led Monochrome Layout
nodes.rationale: Hierarchy is carried entirely by type scale, weight and greyscale value on a white canvas: near-black headings, mid-grey body, lighter grey metadata. No shadows, no card borders, no background tints except the single blue contact card. Dividers are 1px hairlines at roughly 8-10% opacity. Constraint worth preserving: adding a new colour or elevation breaks the system.

nodes.label: Compact rail
nodes.rationale: The shell keeps its expanded outer width so the main column absorbs the freed 136px; that keeps the content's right edge still while the left edge moves.

nodes.label: Light and dark color tokens
nodes.rationale: Every token has a light value in :root and a dark value in :root[data-theme=dark] under the same names, so components read the token and never branch on theme.

nodes.label: Desktop compact rail
nodes.rationale: One shared progress value drives width, labels, character exit and icon centering, so a mid-transition reversal keeps live position and velocity.

nodes.label: Shared rail progress value
nodes.rationale: A single spring value shared by all rail geometry avoids desynchronized sub-animations during rapid reversals.

nodes.label: Theme toggle
nodes.rationale: The glyph swaps from the same data-theme attribute that swaps tokens, so the control renders correctly before hydration.

nodes.label: README interaction notes
nodes.rationale: The rail collapses to 72px as you scroll and reopens at the top, a detail that differs from the manual toggle recorded in DESIGN.md and the release checklist.

nodes.label: Projects page
nodes.rationale: Named separately from Home's selected-work section so a future dedicated page does not get conflated with the previews.

nodes.label: Agreed first release
nodes.rationale: Home and About ship first and the Projects page is deferred because it has not been designed yet, so project navigation must stay static rather than promise a destination that does not exist.

nodes.rationale: Identify and explain reconsideration of an existing ADR before proposing a contradictory decision.

nodes.rationale: Use root CONTEXT.md as vocabulary and docs/adr as numbered architectural decisions.

nodes.label: Home and About visual system
nodes.rationale: White space, dark text, restrained cobalt and cover artwork already carried the pages, so the system records what exists rather than introducing a new world.

nodes.label: Compact side menu
nodes.rationale: A single critically damped spring replaces separate clip, fade and perspective transitions, and an inverse transform layer keeps glyphs and the close target unstretched.

nodes.label: Focus-ring clipping finding
nodes.rationale: At 200 percent text the scroll region clipped Home's top focus border, so 8px block-start padding, scroll padding, and target scroll margins were added because focus indicators must stay visible when keyboard navigation scrolls a control into view.

nodes.label: Mask and elevation split finding
nodes.rationale: When the popup owned both the reveal clip and the overflow mask, the close target sat flush against the clipped edge; moving the mask to an inner surface and shadow to an outer wrapper gives the control and its outline clearance.

nodes.label: Mobile side menu interface review
nodes.rationale: Reviewed with better-interface plus all six owning skills; the review covers accessibility, layout, writing, typography, colors, and UI, and records implemented replacements rather than open findings.

nodes.rationale: A large dark circle holding an up-right arrow, sitting at the right edge of the banner. It reads as a link rather than a button label, keeps the banner copy short, and provides a target large enough to animate toward the cursor.

The local time hints at working-hours overlap for an international audience; social icons stay monochrome so they never outshout the contact banner.

nodes.norm_label: identity lockup: name, role line, mascot avatar
nodes.rationale: Name in heavy sans with a two-tone role sentence ('Alan Sahlan / is a product designer') states who and what in one glance, while the 3D character mascot plus a small blue penguin mark add personality that a headshot would not.

nodes.label: Intro Headline and Positioning Copy
nodes.rationale: Headline 'From the first flow to the final component.' claims end-to-end ownership in one line; the paragraph underneath names the stages (research, wireframes, prototypes) and states a preference for behaviour, scale, and buildability over surface appearance. Together they pre-empt the 'is this person only visual?' objection.

nodes.label: "Have something in mind?" Magnetic Contact Banner
nodes.norm_label: "have something in mind?" magnetic contact banner
nodes.rationale: A wide pale-blue rounded panel anchoring the bottom of the content column, pairing a large question headline with a low-commitment line ('A project, a role, or a good conversation'). The panel is large, colored, and unmissable but contains no form fields, lowering the cost of the click; 'magnetic' refers to the pointer-following behavior of the arrow button in the live build.

nodes.label: Muted Neutral Palette with Soft Accent Panels
nodes.norm_label: muted neutral palette with soft accent panels
nodes.rationale: Near-white page, ink-black type, one blue reserved for links and the role line, and pale blue or grey fills for panels. Color is spent on meaning (accent, active state, banner) rather than decoration, which keeps the photographic project cards as the loudest thing on screen.

nodes.label: Primary Navigation List with Active Home Pill
nodes.norm_label: primary navigation list with active home pill
nodes.rationale: Only two destinations (Home, Know me better), each with a small line icon, and the current page marked by a soft grey pill rather than a color change. The short list signals a small, deliberately shallow site, and the pill gives state feedback without adding visual noise.

nodes.label: Project Preview Card Pair Above the Fold
nodes.norm_label: project preview card pair above the fold
nodes.rationale: Two side-by-side photographic cards with rounded corners, each showing a product in context (a pet-care app, a food-ordering app), chosen over abstract UI crops so the work is legible before any text is read. The asymmetry in subject matter signals range across consumer domains.

nodes.label: See My Resume Secondary Pill
nodes.rationale: A pale grey pill directly under the primary CTA captures the recruiter intent that 'Get in touch' does not serve, without competing for attention.

nodes.label: Theme Toggle and Carousel Arrows
nodes.rationale: Two circular icon controls pinned to the bottom-left of the sidebar: chevrons for paging project previews and a moon glyph for dark mode. They sit below the CTA stack so utility controls never interrupt the identity-to-contact reading order.

nodes.norm_label: sticky sidebar and content two-column layout
nodes.rationale: A fixed narrow left rail carrying identity and navigation against a wide scrolling content column keeps the person and the contact action permanently visible while case-study content changes, and the generous white space around both columns keeps the page reading as editorial rather than dashboard.

nodes.label: Curated Taste As Portfolio Signal
nodes.rationale: Games, an album, a film, and a fantasy novel are mixed in one row with no category labels. The point is breadth of reference, not the individual titles, so the content choice is doing the argument that labels would otherwise have to make.

nodes.label: Experience Entry Header
nodes.rationale: Company name in bold sans, role underneath in muted grey, date range pushed to the far right in a warm tan. Three separate alignment points on one row, so the entry scans as who / what / when without labels.

nodes.label: Media Shelf Strip
nodes.rationale: A single horizontal row of cover art (game box, album, film, book) used as a low-effort personality section. Everything is one size class and one baseline, so the row reads as an object shelf rather than a content grid.

nodes.label: Pull Quote Card
nodes.rationale: Right-aligned tinted panel with a leading vertical rule, a Geralt of Rivia line, and a small attribution. It occupies the empty right half created by the short experience heading on the left, and the vertical rule does the anchoring that a border or shadow would otherwise do.

nodes.label: Blue Accent Ring And Card
nodes.rationale: One cool blue is used for two jobs in the frame: the tinted quote panel and the hover ring on the active shelf item. Reusing a single accent instead of introducing a hover color keeps the section calm while still marking exactly one active element.

nodes.label: Hover Lift With Backing Card
nodes.rationale: On hover the item straightens, scales up, and a white rounded card grows behind it so the tilted cover no longer floats unanchored. The backing card does the affordance work: it reads as 'pick something up', matching the section's microcopy, and it gives a predictable click target around an irregular rotated image.

nodes.label: Section Header With Handwritten Aside
nodes.rationale: Bold statement set in a geometric sans, then a small italic serif aside ('Pick something up.') placed low and to the right of it. The aside is the interaction instruction, so it is styled as an aside rather than a second heading, which keeps the hierarchy to one real title.

nodes.label: Tilted Scatter Layout
nodes.rationale: Each cover sits at a different small rotation and slightly different vertical offset. The imperfection is what sells 'things I keep coming back to' as belongings on a shelf instead of a uniform product carousel. Uniform tilt would read as a template; varied tilt reads as handled objects.

nodes.label: Blue Blob Mascot Character
nodes.rationale: An amorphous saturated-blue shape with two small white oval eyes and a small notch at the top. Deliberately low-detail so it survives being squashed, and so it reads as a character without illustrating a specific object.

nodes.label: Hero Intro Statement Line
nodes.rationale: A single inline sentence ("Alan Sahlan is a product designer") reads as one continuous line instead of a stacked heading plus subtitle, so the name and role are parsed in one glance and the mascot can sit on the same baseline.

nodes.label: Pressed Blob Deformation State
nodes.rationale: The blob is wider and flatter than its rest silhouette, as if pushed down, giving tactile feedback on press. Squash rather than scale keeps the shape readable and signals physical weight without any shadow or outline.

nodes.label: Blob Pressed State Reference Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Captured as a visual reference of the pressed/active state of the site's blob mascot, to be reproduced in the hero intro rather than invented from scratch.

nodes.label: Text-Left Mascot-Right Baseline Alignment
nodes.rationale: Copy occupies the left two thirds and the blob sits flush right, vertically centered on the text block with a small gap. The asymmetry keeps the line from looking like a centered hero banner and leaves the mascot hanging into whitespace.

nodes.label: Mascot As Interactive Affordance
nodes.rationale: The mascot is decorative and clickable at once, so a pressed state is documented as a product surface rather than a brand illustration. This forces the hero layout to reserve real space and hit area for it instead of treating it as background art.

nodes.label: Two-Tone Inline Typography
nodes.rationale: Name in near-black heavy weight, connective words in mid-gray, and the role in saturated blue. Emphasis comes from weight and color rather than size, keeping the line typographically flat and calm. The blue role doubles as the only color accent and implies the role text is the interactive/emphasized token.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Content-Left Action-Right Layout
nodes.rationale: Text stack left, single action far right, with a wide empty middle. The gap is intentional breathing room that makes the card feel unhurried and keeps the CTA from competing with the headline. Vertical centering of the button against the text block keeps the card balanced despite the asymmetry.

nodes.label: Film Recommendation Microcopy
nodes.rationale: Supporting line "A film recommendation is a perfectly good reason." in muted blue-gray, set well below the headline. It removes the pressure of having a professional pretext by naming a trivial one, which lowers the cost of reaching out.

nodes.label: Low-Friction Invitation Pattern
nodes.rationale: Persona-driven contact section: casual question, permission-giving microcopy, and a single minimal action. Together they reduce the social cost of contacting the site owner, which suits a personal site where the goal is conversation rather than lead capture.

nodes.label: Circular Arrow CTA Button
nodes.rationale: Solid near-black circle with a white 45-degree up-right arrow, pinned to the right edge and vertically centered. Icon-only and unlabeled, so it reads as a deliberate secondary action with a large hit area rather than a loud primary button; the diagonal arrow signals leaving the page for an external destination.

nodes.label: Contact CTA Card (lavender surface)
nodes.rationale: Wide, short two-column card with a soft lavender-blue fill (#eef1fb range) and large rounded corners. The tinted surface separates the contact block from the page background without a border or shadow, keeping the invitation visually quiet and warm rather than salesy.

nodes.label: "Say hi?" Headline
nodes.rationale: Oversized near-black display type (roughly 40px, tight tracking, geometric sans) dominates the left third. A two-word question instead of "Contact" or "Get in touch" makes the section read as a friendly invitation and carries the whole hierarchy on its own.

nodes.label: Magnetic Hover Interaction
nodes.rationale: The file name (contact-magnetic-preview) indicates the static frame is a reference for a magnetic cursor effect where the circular button drifts toward the pointer on hover. The isolated circular button exists precisely because a small round target is the natural subject for that attraction motion.

nodes.label: Blue Chat Bubble Availability Indicator
nodes.rationale: A small saturated blue speech-bubble glyph sits beside the name as the only colour accent in the rail, signalling that the designer is reachable without spending a text line on it.

nodes.label: In-Context Device Mockup Imagery
nodes.rationale: Each tile places screens inside a photographed scene (desk, beach resort, studio, cafe table) rather than on a neutral backdrop, so work reads as product-in-the-world and the grid carries visual variety without labels.

nodes.label: Generous Whitespace and Hairline Section Dividers
nodes.norm_label: generous whitespace and hairline section dividers
nodes.rationale: Sections are separated by large vertical gaps and thin one-pixel rules instead of cards or boxes, so the page reads as an editorial document and the eye is paced rather than bounded.

nodes.label: Pill Button System (Filled Black Primary, Soft Grey Secondary)
nodes.norm_label: pill button system (filled black primary, soft grey secondary)
nodes.rationale: Only two button weights exist: one filled black pill for the single primary action (Get in touch) and soft grey pills for everything secondary. Shape rather than colour does the hierarchy work.

nodes.label: Editorial Split Layout (Persistent Rail + Wide Content Column)
nodes.norm_label: editorial split layout (persistent rail + wide content column)
nodes.rationale: A narrow identity rail stays fixed on the left while the work column runs wide to the right. It keeps who-this-is always on screen, gives imagery room to breathe, and replaces a conventional top nav with a personal masthead.
